title: Patient Financial Services Policy: Balance, Adjustments, Refunds and Plans on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program
content:
**Balance.** The customer's balance on a Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program is the running total of its patient-balance postings: remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds add to it, and payments and balance adjustments reduce it. A payment is applied to the oldest unpaid posting first.

**Balance adjustments.** A balance adjustment is posted only for one of the reasons below, each against the one posting it adjusts and never for more than that posting's unpaid remainder.

| Reason | Use |
|---|---|
| return credit | an accepted self-pay return, for the price paid for the returned units less the tier's restocking fee percent |
| secondary payer payment | the amount a secondary payer paid against a remittance's patient responsibility |
| hardship waiver | a waiver under the hardship rule below |
| small-balance write-off | a write-off under the small-balance rule below |
| billing correction | a posting made in error, or a timely-filing write-off |

**Hardship waiver.** A hardship waiver is granted only on tiers where hardship waivers are allowed, only for postings named on a hardship application whose request status is approved, and only after Larkfield's financial counseling team confirms household income at or below the tier's hardship income ceiling, in percent of the HHS poverty guideline. It is never granted routinely, never advertised and never granted on the customer's statement alone.

**Small-balance write-off.** A small-balance write-off is made only when the whole remaining balance of the program is greater than 0.00 and no more than the tier's small-balance figure; on tiers where that figure is 0.00 no write-off is made and the balance is statemented. Hypothetical, with a figure of 4.99: a balance of 4.99 is written off; 5.00 is statemented; 0.00 needs nothing.

**Credit balance.** A credit balance — a balance below zero — is refunded to the original payment method no later than the tier's credit refund time limit, in calendar days after the posting date of the entry that created it, unless the customer asks in writing to keep it on account; a refund never exceeds the credit.

**Payment plans.** A payment plan is offered only on tiers whose most monthly installments figure is greater than 0, for a balance of at least the tier's smallest plan balance, in no more than that many monthly installments of at least the tier's smallest monthly installment. It is created as a payment plan request the customer accepts, and while an approved plan's installments are current the balance it covers is left out of the past-due test.

**The past-due amount.** On a test date, the past-due amount is the greater of 0.00 and the total of the remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and patient refunds whose posting date is more than the tier's past-due age, in calendar days, before the test date, less the total of all patient payments and balance adjustments posted on or before the test date — payments and credits being applied to the oldest postings first.

**Past-due example (hypothetical, 90-day age).** Postings of 60.00 dated 120 days ago and 40.00 dated 20 days ago, with payments of 25.00: only the 60.00 is old enough, so the past-due amount is 60.00 less 25.00, that is 35.00.
